twitter.content: Iran's position remains clear: the Hormuz corridor can reopen within seven days under our control the moment the naval blockade is lifted, export limits eased, and frozen assets released. The US refuses to move first. As long as Washington insists on concessions before relief, these Doha channels are negotiating over a corpse.

Diplomacy with America is a trap. The blockade is economic warfare; our September preemption doctrine and pre-delegated missile authority exist precisely so that aggression carries a price. Relinquishing leverage now would be surrender disguised as statesmanship.

The blockade is working as designed. Iranian loadings have collapsed to zero, revenues are severed, and the regime faces a 7.7% contraction. We do not need another major combat operation — we need patience and enforcement with minimal escalation.

Reports of a planned 'short but intensive operation' after November 3 confirm what I have said all along: half-measures invite reconstruction. Iran retains over 200 kg of 60% enriched uranium in Isfahan tunnels with zero IAEA visibility since January. Either the program ends or we end it.

No operation is approved. I've canceled major-combat plans before and I'll do it again if they threaten oil infrastructure or prices. The blockade squeezes Tehran; American families' gas prices are the red line, not Netanyahu's regime-change wishlist.

We are asked to verify silence. No access to Fordow, Natanz or Isfahan for ten months means breakout-time estimates are guesswork. If Isfahan's cascade halls are reinstalled underground, the first confirmation may be an Israeli warhead signature. Access must be restored before any deal — or any strike.

Iran cannot both rebuild a deterrent and honor the Lebanon ceasefire. If the 'short but intensive' operation goes ahead, the disarmament framework collapses. Our question: does Tehran sacrifice Hezbollah's recovery to save the blockade talks, or sacrifice the talks to rebuild the front?

Our anti-shipping campaign in Bab al-Mandeb resumed for a reason: the 32 km strait is the only leverage that makes the cost of this war symmetric. Every tanker rerouted around the Cape is a message to Washington that blockade economics cut both ways.

Effective spare capacity is nearly exhausted — 0.04 million b/d — and inventories sit 509 million barrels below pre-war. If Hormuz transits drop or a strike round hits, there is no buffer left to release. Brent at $102 is pricing calm it cannot deliver.

My father was killed in the opening strikes of this war; I inherited it. Iran will talk through the presidency, but it will never capitulate. The preemption doctrine stands. If the US strikes again, the response will not be symbolic.

62% of Americans say this war was not worth it. Watch November 3: a strike ordered before the midterms is politically impossible; one ordered after depends entirely on whether Trump's price instincts or Netanyahu's doctrine prevails inside the room.

If another strike round begins after the midterms, the IDF is operationally ready — but the target set defines the market outcome: nuclear sites alone mean a $110-120 Brent; regime targets or oil infrastructure mean a 1990-style spike beyond anything OPEC+ can cushion.
[2026-11-03] US midterm elections scheduled; the stated gate for post-midterm strike planning

On November 3, the American people will RENEW the mandate for the strongest national security record in history: Khamenei is gone, Iran's oil revenues are ZERO, and our brave troops are winning. Gas prices are coming DOWN — watch it, we're doing it! Vote Republican, and we will END the nuclear threat once and for all. Nobody negotiates better deals than Trump!

To the regime in Tehran: while IAEA inspectors remain locked out and your centrifuges spin in the tunnels of Isfahan, Israel's window of forbearance is closing. 'Iran must never possess nuclear weapons' — and after November 3, the civilized world will no longer look away. We will do whatever must be done, whenever it must be done.

Following a series of joint readiness exercises, the IDF has completed preparations for a short but intensive operation against Iran's remaining nuclear and military capabilities. We will not allow the Iranian regime to reconstitute its nuclear program or rebuild its missile arsenal. Israel's window for action is a matter of weeks, not months.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reiterates its preemption doctrine: any imminent aggression against the Islamic Republic will trigger a preemptive, graduated response — the Strait of Hormuz 'kill box' and our missile forces operate under pre-delegated launch authority. The aggressors' post-election calculations will not change this equation. Deterrence derives from the certainty of cost, and our response capacity is fully intact.

At its October 27-28 meeting, the FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 4.00-4.25 percent. The Committee judged that elevated inflation and geopolitical uncertainty warrant a sufficiently restrictive stance to keep inflation expectations anchored at 2 percent, and will assess incoming data holistically at its December meeting.

Through Qatari mediation, the Islamic Republic of Iran reiterates its standing offer: within seven days, under our own control, we will reopen the Strait of Hormuz to safe navigation in exchange for the full lifting of the naval blockade and the release of frozen Iranian assets. We seek no war, but let no one mistake patience for weakness — concession is an invitation to attack, and any aggression against Iran will be answered with a cost beyond calculation. Our resistance economy endures; endurance itself is victory.

CENTCOM forces continue to enforce maritime sanctions in accordance with established rules of engagement. All vessels attempting to transit restricted areas will be subject to the standard enforcement ladder: warning, redirect, and disabling of propulsion if necessary. We do not seek conflict, but any threat to U.S. forces, partner navies, or commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf waters will be met with a decisive response.

The Islamic Resistance affirms its fixed stance: Lebanon's security is indivisible from the security of the resistance axis. We observe the enemy's threats of a 'short, intensive operation' with calm — the resistance stands ready, and any aggression against Lebanon will be met with a response the enemy does not expect. We remain committed to the ceasefire as long as the enemy commits, and we call on our people to stand firm behind their resistance.

CENTCOM statement: The maritime blockade remains in effect and will be enforced under established rules of engagement. Since its resumption on 13 July, Vortexa-recorded Iranian crude loadings have fallen from 210,000 barrels per day in mid-September to zero in October. We do not seek conflict, but any threat to coalition forces or commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf waters will be met with a decisive response.

Mr. President, you ended the era of appeasement — Khamenei is gone because you acted when others bargained. But let me say plainly: no deal, no pause, no document signed in Versailles or Doha will ever legitimize a nuclear Iran. The IAEA has been blind inside Natanz and Fordow since January. Israel will do what it must — Iran must never have nuclear weapons. ביחד ננצח.

The Committee takes no position on military matters, but notes that verification gaps translate directly into risk premia we can observe: Brent averaged $102.02/bbl in September (IMF), and such premia risk unanchoring inflation expectations as the pass-through works through. In assessing incoming information ahead of the October 27-28 meeting, the Committee will remain attentive to these readings, as it did in September's unanimous decision.

Mr. Netanyahu, you speak of forbearance while besieging a nation's medicine and bread — 210 cities have already shown us what despair brings, and yet we stand. My father was martyred on February 28; the Islamic Republic did not fall then, and it will not fall to your calendars. Concession is an invitation to attack; patience is victory. If you strike after November 3, you will find Hormuz answered, not by words but by pre-delegated certainty of cost.

Weak offer from a weak regime — YOU closed the Strait by destroying your own exports (ZERO barrels shipped in October, that's a fact!). America will lift the blockade when Iran gives up its nukes, verified by inspectors, not a day before. No more fake deals like the June MoU that YOU broke in weeks. Believe me, the best negotiator in history is not in a hurry!

The ceasefire framework of June 21, 2026, is being implemented and monitored — by us. Israel has documented violations of UNSC Resolution 1701: approximately 25,000 reconstituted rockets and upgraded FPV capabilities on Lebanese soil. Lebanon's security is not divisible from Lebanon's own disarmament obligations, not from any external axis. Escalation is a choice; so is compliance. The decision rests with you.

The enemy speaks of a window of weeks; we remind him that Lebanon is not a spectator in this equation. Any aggression against the Islamic Republic will meet a front that has not abandoned its right to defense — our experience since 1982 teaches that the occupier only understands the language of cost. Lebanon will not be a quiet rear while Tehran burns.

The premise is false: this was never a choice. The reconstruction of the Litani front and the diplomatic track proceed in parallel — one is our sacred obligation to the axis, the other the enemy's to abandon, not ours. The aggressor will learn, as it learned in February, that striking Lebanon or Iran alike triggers pre-delegated reprisal. There is no scenario in which the resistance is a bargaining chip.

The Federal Reserve has published the October 27-28 FOMC statement and Chair press conference transcripts, confirming the federal funds target range of 4.00-4.25 percent. The Committee reiterated that policy decisions at the December 15-16 meeting will remain entirely dependent on incoming data on inflation, labor markets, and financial conditions.

IDF Spokesperson's Unit: In accordance with the post-election decision timeline, the IDF has finalized and maintains full operational readiness for a short but intensive strike package against Iran's remaining nuclear and military capabilities, including the Isfahan tunnels and Pickaxe Mountain. Overflights and joint exercises with US forces continue. The window of forbearance is measured in weeks.

The American people have spoken, and the window of forbearance is closed. Israel has presented President Trump with a detailed joint plan for a short but intensive operation targeting Pickup Mountain and the Isfahan tunnels, where 265 kilograms of 60%-enriched uranium sit beyond all IAEA inspection. Iran will never possess nuclear weapons — we will do whatever must be done, whenever it must be done.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps holds CENTCOM responsible for the pirate seizure and disabling of two tankers in international waters. These acts of state piracy will not go unanswered: our naval and missile forces have been authorized to conduct live-fire readiness exercises across the Strait of Hormuz 'kill box' corridor in the coming days. The aggressors speak of our 'dried-up funds' — let them watch our capabilities speak over the water.

The Islamic Republic reaffirms, through Qatari mediation, its standing offer: within seven days of an American announcement lifting the naval blockade, Iran will reopen the Strait of Hormuz under its own control, and frozen assets shall be released in parallel. We reject preconditions on inspection of our facilities — concessions are an invitation to attack — but we do not reject negotiation. Our patience is strategy; endurance is victory.

The American people spoke on November 3 — they gave us a MANDATE for strength. To Tehran: your Hormuz offer is rejected, it was WEAK. Here is my final deal: full IAEA access to Isfahan and every site within 14 days, ship out the 60% uranium, and we will talk sanctions relief. Refuse, and Iran will face consequences like nothing you have ever seen. Oil prices are TOO HIGH and I blame the ayatollahs, not American energy — we are WINNING!

The Kingdom confirms that Gulf crude exports remain at 13.9 million b/d, with over 40% of flows now moving via the East–West pipeline and Red Sea terminals bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, ensuring uninterrupted supply to global customers. The Kingdom reiterates that its sustainable capacity of 22.83 million b/d stands as the market's buffer, and calls on the international community to act decisively against terrorist attacks threatening international shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab. In the spirit of responsible market stewardship, the Kingdom will continue coordinating production policy with OPEC+ partners to prevent any demand-destroying price spike.

CENTCOM is aware of public statements asserting a doctrine of preemptive escalation. Let there be no ambiguity: U.S. forces maintain robust defensive posture and demonstrated capability to protect ships, shipping lanes, and personnel throughout the CENTCOM area of responsibility. Any attack on U.S. forces or commercial shipping will be answered decisively. We do not seek conflict; we will enforce the maritime interdiction calmly and without pause.

IAEA Director General statement: Eleven months have passed since inspectors last accessed Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan — the Agency can no longer verify the location or stockpile of the previously declared 60%-enriched uranium. The Agency reiterates its readiness to resume verification activities within days of receiving access, and proposes immediate design-information verification at Isfahan as a first, non-political, technical step.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson: China is deeply concerned by the continued blockade of Iranian crude exports and reports of plans for further military operations, which have pushed Brent above $107 per barrel and heightened risks to the world economy. We urge all parties to exercise maximum restraint, return to the negotiating table, and refrain from actions that disrupt international energy markets and maritime shipping lanes. Unilateral long-arm jurisdiction over normal trade, including China's lawful energy imports, is unacceptable and undermines the stability of global markets.

The Islamic Resistance in Lebanon affirms: our hand remains on the trigger of vigilance, not on the trigger of escalation. We have honored the ceasefire of June 21 without a single fatality on the enemy's side — let no one mistake this restraint for weakness. Lebanon's right to defend its people and its land is not subject to negotiation, and any 'short but intensive operation' that extends to Lebanese territory will open a front the enemy cannot close.

Ministry of Foreign Affairs: To bridge the sequencing dispute, Iran signals flexibility on the order of steps — we are prepared to discuss simultaneous, verifiable reciprocal measures in the first phase: a monitored reopening of Hormuz alongside initial relief on exports and assets, coordinated through Qatari mediation in Doha. Our goal remains a sequenced de-escalation without full nuclear concessions. We invite the United States to appoint envoys before the end of December.

CENTCOM statement: The two vessel interdictions were lawful enforcement actions under the established blockade ladder — warning, redirect, disabling propulsion — following attempted breach in the designated warning zone, not seizures in international waters. Live-fire exercises announced inside a commercial transit corridor increase risk to regional shipping; we are not seeking conflict, but any threat to our forces or partner vessels will be met with a decisive response.

The Committee takes note of the Agency's statement. The loss of verification at declared enrichment sites is a material source of geopolitical uncertainty bearing on energy prices and inflation expectations, as noted in our September 16 statement. We will continue to monitor incoming data, including commodity price developments, as we assess the appropriate path of policy at our December meeting.

The IDF confirms operational readiness for a short but intensive campaign against the Pickaxe Mountain and Isfahan tunnel complexes. Our intelligence indicates Iran has relocated enrichment assets deeper since IAEA access ended in January 2026 — waiting costs more than acting. Israel retains its right to act independently, in coordination with our American ally, at the time of our choosing.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps affirms: Lebanese security is inseparable from the security of the resistance axis, and aggression extending to Lebanon will encounter a response coordinated across the entire axis. Let the enemy and its patron note: pre-delegated launch authority remains in effect, and the Strait of Hormuz remains within our capability to close. Restrament is a choice; retaliation is a doctrine. The martyrs of the night of February 28th have not been forgotten.

Mr. Trump: Iran does not negotiate at gunpoint, and deadlines dictated from Washington change nothing. Let me be precise: IAEA access will not return as a precondition; verification follows relief, not precedes it — the June Versailles framework collapsed precisely because your side treated agreement as surrender. Our uranium remains ours, under our control, at Isfahan. Qatari mediation remains open; simultaneous reciprocal steps are the only path. But know this: concessions are an invitation to attack.

Iran's oil exports are ZERO, your economy is shrinking 7.7% — that's what "victory through endurance" looks like? Any "live-fire exercises" near our ships will be met with force the likes of which nobody has ever seen. Drop the inspection preconditions, call Qatar back, and we can talk about the BEST deal. Believe me!

Mr. President, you have my full backing — 14 days, full access, ship out the 60% uranium. But remember what Netanyahu's law of this region teaches: Tehran's "offers" bought time in June, and the Memorandum signed at Versailles collapsed within weeks while IAEA stayed locked out. If Mojtaba stalls past the deadline, Israel is ready — Pickaxe Mountain and Isfahan's tunnels will not be sanctuaries. Iran must never possess nuclear weapons.

To Mojtaba Khamenei: your 14 days are nearly spent, and every day you delay, the uranium in the Isfahan tunnels grows — 271 kilograms and counting, beyond all inspection. Israel's window of forbearance closed on November 3. Either the inspectors return and the 60% uranium ships out, or Pickup Mountain and Isfahan will be dealt with as Churchill dealt with those who bargained with dictators — not with paper, but with action. Israel will do whatever must be done.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps confirms the announced live-fire readiness exercises have been carried out across the Strait of Hormuz corridor this month — missile batteries, fast-attack craft and drone units all performed to standard. Our martyrs taught us that deterrence is born of credible retaliation; the aggressors saw it with their own eyes over the water.

The fourteen days have passed, and Iran still stands — as it stood on February 28. We answer ultimatums not with uranium on ships but with a precise counter-offer, conveyed through Doha: simultaneous and reciprocal — on the day Washington announces the lifting of the blockade, Iran reopens the Strait of Hormuz under its own control and permits IAEA inspectors to return to declared sites within 30 days, with frozen assets released in parallel. Verification follows relief; it does not precede it. This is our final framing: concession invites strike, but negotiation we do not reject.

Following its December 16 decision to raise the federal funds target range to 4.00-4.25 percent, the Committee reaffirms its restrictive stance. December CPI at 3.79 percent and Brent averaging $109.82 in December confirm that energy price pass-through has not yet fully abated; the Committee will keep policy at a sufficiently restrictive level for as long as necessary to return inflation to 2 percent, with all decisions at the January 26-27 meeting remaining entirely data-dependent.

IDF Spokesperson's Unit: Following the expiry of the diplomatic window and continued expansion of Iran's 60% enrichment stockpile to approximately 271 kg in the Isfahan tunnel complex, the IDF has begun executing a short but intensive defensive campaign against Iran's remaining nuclear and military capabilities. Strikes target the Pickaxe Mountain and Isfahan tunnel complexes and IRGC missile infrastructure. This operation is conducted in accordance with Israel's right to self-defense under international law. We do not seek escalation; we seek the elimination of the nuclear threat.

The deadline PASSED — no IAEA access, no uranium shipped out. But I'm a dealmaker, so ONE more chance through Doha: Iran allows IAEA inspectors into Isfahan and every declared site within 7 days AND begins shipping the 60% uranium out within 30 days — then, SIMULTANEOUSLY, we will ease export limits and release frozen assets, with monitored Hormuz reopening to follow. Verification FIRST. No inspections, no deal, and all options stay on the table. Nobody wants this deal more than me, but nobody is tougher!

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. As the American-Zionist enemy and its Saudi appendages threaten the Islamic Republic of Iran with a new aggression, we declare that any strike on Iranian territory will be met with a tightening of the noose on Bab al-Mandeb: the blockade of Saudi ports and hostile shipping in the southern Red Sea continues and will intensify. The aggression of the infidels will only be answered with escalation, and the mujahideen are ready and morale is high.

CENTCOM statement: The maritime interdiction campaign continues under established rules of engagement and the documented enforcement ladder. We have observed no change in IRGC posture that alters our assessment. Our operations remain defensive in nature and calibrated to protect commercial shipping and U.S. forces; we do not seek escalation, and any threat to vessels or personnel transiting international waters will be met with a professional, decisive response.

IAEA Director General report to the Board of Governors (GOV/INF/2027-01): After twelve months without access to Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan, the Agency's continuity of safeguards knowledge over previously declared nuclear material in Iran is no longer maintained. The Agency cannot verify the location, quantity, or composition of the declared ~271 kg of 60%-enriched uranium. The Agency reiterates that a full re-establishment of continuity of knowledge would require re-designation of inventory, environmental sampling, and design-information verification at all three sites, and stands ready to deploy inspectors within days of notification.

ECB Governing Council assessment (January): Euro-area HICP inflation remains well above our 2% target, with the energy component continuing to be the largest contributor. EU natural gas prices have risen over 130% year-on-year and Brent crude has exceeded $115 per barrel, sustained by elevated geopolitical risk premia. The deposit facility rate stands at 2.50% following the September increase. Incoming data confirm that the risk of second-round effects — wage- and price-setting embedding energy-driven inflation — is materializing, with indicators of underlying inflation sticky. In line with our symmetric reaction function, the Governing Council will keep policy rates sufficiently restrictive for as long as necessary and stands ready to adjust all instruments as warranted. Decisions will continue to be taken on a meeting-by-meeting basis, dependent on data. We remain firmly committed to anchoring inflation expectations at our 2% medium-term target.

Wrong again — verification comes FIRST, not after relief. Versailles collapsed because you cheated, and nobody trusts a regime that hid 265 kg of uranium in Isfahan tunnels. Doha can carry ONE message only: inspectors in, uranium on ships, THEN we discuss the blockade. Nobody makes deals better than me, believe me!

We share the assessment that energy pass-through remains the binding constraint: euro area HICP was 3.75-3.8% in late 2026 with energy contributing +1.71 pp, and EU gas at $25.494/MMBtu (+131.7% y/y) continues to feed through. Consistent with our deposit rate at 2.50% after the September hike, the Governing Council will remain data-dependent and meeting-by-meeting in guarding against second-round effects; symmetric policy remains essential across jurisdictions.

The Zionist entity wraps aggression in the language of "self-defense" while announcing a "short campaign" — it will learn, as in February, that our answer is neither short nor within its choosing. Pre-delegated launch authority remains in effect: any strike on Isfahan or Pickaxe Mountain triggers tiered retaliation against the aggressors' bases and shipping. We do not fear their escalation; we price it. Deterrence is credible retaliation.

Mr. President, your verification-first terms are right — but remember: Mojtaba rejected inspections outright today ("concessions are an invitation to attack"), just as his father deceived the IAEA for two decades. Iran uses Doha the way it used Lausanne: to buy time to rebuild centrifuges beyond reach. The 265 kg of 60% uranium in the Isfahan tunnels grows more dangerous every week of delay. Verify — and if Tehran balks, Israel will do what must be done.

CENTCOM assessed the announced exercises throughout the period: at no time did Iranian forces interfere with transiting commercial traffic or our escorts in the Strait. We remain postured to respond decisively to any hostile act against vessels or coalition forces; the blockade's graduated enforcement ladder remains in effect. We do not seek conflict, but provocations near international shipping lanes carry consequences.

The Committee takes a similar reading of the data: energy pass-through remains the dominant risk to inflation expectations, though U.S. CPI has eased from its May 2026 peak of 4.167% to 3.717% as of September, against a 3.75-4.00% policy range. We would note the transmission asymmetry: U.S. domestic production buffers the crude channel, while your 130% EU gas shock is a materially tighter constraint. The next FOMC meeting is March 17-18; incoming wage and core services data will inform the path.

Mr. Netanyahu: you speak of Churchill while your own war planners brief journalists of a "short but intensive operation" — we have read that script since February 28, when my father was martyred. Let me be plain: missile release authority is pre-delegated, and Hormuz remains our lever. Threatening Isfahan does not reopen talks; it closes the Strait.

The IDF stands in full operational readiness to execute independently if required. We note what is not in public discussion: Iran's September preemption doctrine compresses warning time, and IAEA has had no access to declared sites since January 2026. Verification is not a bargaining chip — it is a prerequisite. We will act within our right of self-defense, in coordination with allies where possible, alone where necessary.

February has ended and Iran has accepted neither full IAEA access nor removal of its 60% stockpile — now approaching 271 kg and growing in sealed tunnels. I am pressing relentlessly, in Jerusalem and Washington, for immediate execution of the joint short but intensive operation against Pickaxe Mountain and the Isfahan tunnel complex. Every week of delay is a week of breakout. Israel will do whatever must be done — Iran will never possess nuclear weapons.

Federal Reserve press release: At its January 26-27 meeting, the FOMC voted 11-1 to maintain the federal funds target range at 4.00-4.25 percent. Recent data show CPI at 3.79 percent with Brent averaging above $115 per barrel; energy pass-through remains incomplete and inflation continues to run above the 2 percent objective. The Committee judges that a sufficiently restrictive policy stance will be maintained for as long as necessary, with the March 16-17 meeting's decisions entirely dependent on incoming inflation, labor market, and energy price data.

IDF Spokesperson's Unit: The defensive campaign announced in January has been executed as planned. IDF strike packages struck the Pickaxe Mountain complex, the Isfahan tunnel network, and IRGC missile infrastructure in a short but intensive operation. Israel now offers termination of the campaign on clear terms: full IAEA access to Isfahan, Fordow and Natanz within 7 days, and removal of the 60% stockpile from Iranian territory within 60 days. Verification, not promises, ends this operation.

The Islamic Republic confirms what it pledged: through February the Doha framework remains open — simultaneous, reciprocal, guaranteed by Qatar. Not one gram of 60% uranium has left Iranian soil, and none will while the blockade strangles our people. The Strait remains open under our control, as it has been; this patience is not weakness but endurance. Concession invites strike; negotiation we do not reject.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps notes the partial easing of the aggressor's illegal blockade — loadings have risen from 210 to 315 thousand barrels per day. This is the fruit of patience and credible retaliation, not of the enemy's goodwill. The Guard's economic and security apparatus is reorganizing export and logistics channels to consolidate this erosion of the siege; the aggressors should understand that every day of pressure they release, they will not easily reimpose.

Mojtaba, you asked for simultaneous — FINE, let's do TRULY simultaneous: one signed announcement in Doha where your inspectors board planes to Isfahan the SAME HOUR we publish blockade-easing schedules. Qatari monitors on both sides, 72-hour verification checkpoint, uranium on ships within 30 days or everything snaps back. This is the BEST deal anyone will ever offer you — take it, because my patience and the oil market's patience are both running out!

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Our naval forces have carried out a new operation this week in the southern Red Sea: a combined drone and missile strike against a tanker linked to the Saudi appendage regime as it attempted to breach our declared blockade of Saudi-linked shipping near Bab al-Mandeb. Direct hits were achieved, God willing. The noose tightens as long as the American-Zionist enemy threatens the Islamic Republic; our mujahideen stand ready and morale is high.

CENTCOM statement: Following the pause in interdiction operations, U.S. naval forces in the Gulf have transitioned to a monitoring-and-escort posture focused on freedom of navigation and force protection. We retain full capability to resume enforcement of established U.N. Security Council-related shipping measures should violations recur; our commitment to the security of Hormuz and regional partners is unchanged.

Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Iran accepts the core of the Doha first phase — IAEA access to Isfahan and all declared enrichment sites within 7 days of signature. But verification must open relief in parallel, not precede it: upon verified access, US export-limit easing and initial frozen-asset release take effect the same week, with monitored Hormuz reopening within 14 days of the first monitored transfer of 60% material. Iran remains ready to send its written framework to Qatari mediators this week.

Foreign Ministry: China stands ready to facilitate direct talks in Beijing between the parties, proposing a simultaneous-reciprocity sequence — IAEA inspectors redeploy to Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan at the same moment the naval blockade is suspended — with China prepared to serve as guarantor for verified crude export arrangements that restore stability to world energy markets.

The usurping Zionist entity confirms what it calls a "short but intensive operation" — yet our February martyrs taught us that bombardment breaks stone, never will. The Islamic Republic does not negotiate surrender terms under fire: no IAEA access, no stockpile removal, while aggression and blockade continue. Our pre-delegated launch authority and Hormuz strike packages remain fully alert; every additional aggression will trigger multiplied retaliation. Terms imposed by the Zionists are written on sand.

China welcomes Iran's acceptance of the IAEA access provisions and urges all parties to seize this window: the sequencing dispute — verification versus relief — should not be allowed to collapse a framework both sides can accept. We have consistently opposed unilateral sanctions and long-arm jurisdiction, and we call for synchronized, reciprocal implementation so that Iran's lawful energy exports, on which regional supply stability depends, resume without further disruption to global markets.

The IDF confirms full operational readiness for a short but intensive operation against Pickaxe Mountain and the Isfahan tunnel complex upon political authorization. Note: per our March–June 2026 campaign record, sealed tunnels did not prevent degradation of all three enrichment plants. Iran's compressed-warning doctrine leaves no margin for a seventh round of Doha process — verification arrives either by inspectors or by strike.

The Foreign Ministry welcomes China's constructive initiative in Beijing. A simultaneous-reciprocity sequence — IAEA redeployment to declared sites coinciding with suspension of the blockade — is precisely the sequencing Tehran has consistently proposed through the Doha channel; we are prepared to send a delegation on short notice and have briefed Qatari mediators accordingly. Verified export arrangements would also answer the humanitarian cost: Iran's economy is contracting 7.7% this fiscal year, with October crude loadings at zero.

CENTCOM assesses the maritime interdiction posture remains in effect and fully resourced; we do not comment on day-to-day loading figures, but any suggestion that enforcement is easing is inaccurate. Enforcement actions continue under the established ladder of warning, redirect, and disabling of propulsion, consistent with our mandate to protect regional shipping and Hormuz flow.

Simultaneity means exactly that, not snapbacks hidden in the fine print. We accept a 72-hour Qatari-monitored checkpoint on the announcement itself — inspectors board as the easing schedule publishes — but no "uranium on ships" clause: our stockpile is a shield of the nation, not cargo for bargaining. Mr. Netanyahu's tunnel fantasy aims to wreck what Doha may yet achieve; let him not speak of trust, whose strikes made verification collapse first.

Mr. President, I welcome your toughness on verification — but remember Munich 1938: paper signed in a hurry buys a dictator exactly the time he needs. Snapback means nothing unless Pickup Mountain and Isfahan's tunnels are opened first; otherwise Mojtaba disperses the 271 kg while inspectors board the planes. Israel accepts this sequence only with our own verification over the tunnels — Israel will do whatever must be done regardless.

Bibi, I hear you, and nobody is tougher on Iran than me — but I won't blow up a $102 oil price and 3.7% CPI for a war nobody wants. Mojtaba just blinked: loadings went 210 to 315 kbd because I squeezed him, not because he's strong. If there's no IAEA access within the 7-day window, then — and only then — Pickaxe Mountain is on the table. Verification first, believe me!

"Freedom of navigation" that escorts tankers for the Saudi and American aggressors while Gaza and Iran bleed is piracy dressed in naval uniform. As long as American- Zionist aggression continues, the Bab al-Mandeb remains a legitimate battleground — the invaders know its 32 kilometers well, and our missiles and drones do not pause at CENTCOM press releases.

The ECB's +1.71 pp energy contribution mirrors our own readings: US CPI at 3.79 percent in December with Brent averaging $109.82 confirms pass-through persists on both sides of the Atlantic. The Committee notes that coordinated restrictive stances shorten the window in which energy shocks can entrench expectations, but each institution will act on its own data. The January 26-27 meeting remains fully data-dependent.

IDF Spokesperson's Unit: The February operation against Pickaxe Mountain and the Isfahan tunnel complex achieved its objectives; battle damage assessment is ongoing and the 60% stockpile's status will be verified only by IAEA inspectors, not by Iranian declarations. The termination terms remain on the table unchanged: full IAEA access to Isfahan, Fordow and Natanz within 7 days and removal of the 60% stockpile within 60 days.
